findings.summary: Rule (b) flags suspended hyphens such as `one- or two-line` as a glued bullet marker
findings.evidence: Decision 4: "a glued `-` needs an alphanumeric or sentence-end char right before it", and decision 3 lets a `-` marker be glued "with an optional space". Nothing requires an item head after the marker. So any new prompt line with `one- or two-line`, `pre- and post-verification` or `Rust- and Go-based` has a letter, then `- `, then a word, and matches. Grep finds that exact construct in README.md:3 ("a lazy, one- or two-line request"), docs/design/athena-v0.md:109 and two review docs, so it is ordinary prose in this repository. The producer would be sent back with a finding it can only clear by rewording correct prose. Criterion 3's no-false-positive cases (`1.2. Then`, `*emphasis* note:`, ` - note:` on an unchanged line) do not cover it. The same looseness flags an italic sentence ending in a period followed by text (`*Never do X.* Then`): a `*` glued after a sentence-end char, then a space. Fix: Make rule (b) require an item head after the glued marker, not only a character before it. After a glued or space-joined `-`/`*`, require `<word>:` within 40 chars (the head shape decision 3 already defines for rule (a)) or the head of a base item. Alternatively, allow a letter or digit before a glued `-` only when such a head follows. The y8kr shape `suffice.- deliverables:` still matches either way. Add `one- or two-line notes` and `*Never do X.* Then` to the criterion 3 no-findings test.
findings.location: Plan decision 4 (rule (b) guard) and decision 3; criterion 3 demonstration

findings.summary: The plan says two different things about whether rule (a) checks the character before a head
findings.evidence: The Risks section says rule (a) matches "with a sentence-end or glue check before the head". Decisions 3-5 and step 4 describe rule (a) only as "base head mid-line in a new line not in the base" and put the guards on rule (b) alone. A new line that quotes a base head as an example ("write `- deliverables:` as a list") would be flagged or not depending on which text the producer follows. Fix: State in decision 3 or step 4 whether rule (a) requires a sentence-end or glue character before the matched head (for example: not after a backtick or a space following a word). Pin a quoted-head case in the criterion 3 test.
findings.location: Plan Risks (first item) vs decision 3 / step 4 rule (a)

findings.summary: Indented (nested) list items are not addressed
findings.evidence: The prompts under crates/*/prompts/ are Markdown, and Markdown lists can nest with leading spaces. The plan does not say whether heads are collected from indented items. It also does not say whether "mid-line" means after non-whitespace text, so an item whose only change is its indentation could be reported as joined, or a joined nested item could be missed. Fix: Define heads and "mid-line" on the line with its leading whitespace trimmed (mid-line = after non-whitespace text), and add a re-indent no-findings case and a nested-join case to the tests.
findings.location: Plan decision 3 / step 4 (heads and mid-line detection)

summary: I checked the plan against the snapshot by reading and grepping it. I ran nothing. The named code is all there: REGISTRY, Rule, BaseFn, append_only_problem, glob_matches/segment_matches, watches, check_entry and check_all in mirrors.rs; mirror_drift_in in producer.rs:75-86; check_log and its three tests in athena-cli decisions.rs:218-395; the exhaustive `match entry.rule` and the `drift.mirror == entry.mirror` assertion in athena-cli tests/mirrors.rs; and mirror_job, fixing_on_send_back, athena_source_repo and commit_file in run/tests.rs. Fixing this in the registry is the right origin: it covers the whole class, and the producer loop and the cli test both run the new entries with no new call site. The dependents list matches what I found. The demonstrations drive production entry points with real fixtures, would fail without the new rules, and criterion 7 is shown end to end through the real send-back. Moving the log parser into mirrors.rs (one parser instead of two) is sound: it keeps every message fragment the check_log tests assert, and the D145 heading sits before the pin. D161 is the last entry, so D162 is the right next id. Athena's three scope findings are answered by decision 9: the files are needed to compile, to show criterion 7, and to share the parser. One soundness problem remains. Rule (b)'s guard accepts a glued `-` after any letter or digit even when no item head follows, so a common English construct is sent back as a joined bullet. That is an obvious false positive with a cheap fix, so the verdict is revise.
